technical_errors: MODERATE-HIGH (82): SKILL.md lines 271-283, step 8 — internal self-contradiction. The text states 'the verdict space collapses to two answers' and lists exactly two bullets (mode-documented-behaviour, or tool-bug), then the very next paragraph says '`unspecified-behaviour` remains available and is worth checking honestly' — introducing a third outcome that directly contradicts the preceding sentence's claim of exactly two. A reader skimming the bolded two-item list (a very plausible reading pattern for a reference doc like this) will miss that a third ruling is still live for own-tool comparisons. Fix: change 'collapses to two answers' to something like 'collapses to two answers, plus one honest escape hatch' or otherwise fold unspecified-behaviour into the enumerated list rather than contradicting the count in the next sentence.
verb_honesty: HIGH (90): SKILL.md lines 319-324, step 9 — "Route on the ruling, using the Escalation path slot: ... Then write the entry into the Precedent record, keyed the way that record keys things — including the ones ruled not-comparable..." The agent has only Read, Grep and Glob; it cannot write an entry into an external Precedent record (a database, tracker, or even a plain file — this agent has no Write tool at all). This is a bare verb the agent cannot perform, and it is inconsistent with the SAME skill's own step 6, which correctly treats the Precedent record as read-only ('Grep the Precedent record for the construct name...if the record is not a file that can be read, hand the question to whoever can search it and say the check is pending'). Fix: rephrase as an explicit handoff, e.g. 'ask whoever maintains the Precedent record to add this entry, in the format that record uses' — matching the handoff phrasing used everywhere else in this skill and in the golden references (dv-ral-bringup: 'ask the engineer to run...').
budget_violations: HIGH (85): SKILL.md lines 126-141 (step 1) vs. the budget at lines 98-100. Step 1's second comparability question requires the reader to determine 'Is everything except the tool identical? Same source revision, same defines, same filelist, same options, same library and VIP versions, same seed' — and explicitly branches on it ('If the file sets differ, this is a build difference...; if anything else moved, record ruling: not-comparable and stop'). But the retrieval budget allocates exactly ONE Grep per side for step 1, and that Grep's pattern is fixed to alternate only three specific strings: the tool's version banner, the profile's Run identity string, and the profile's Pass marker (line 98-100, 126-127). None of those three marker types plausibly reveals defines, filelist contents, compile options, or library/VIP version numbers — and the step even acknowledges filelist differences are a distinct, checkable condition ('If the file sets differ...') without giving any mechanism inside the budget to actually see the file sets. There is no Read allocated to step 1 at all, and no handoff phrasing ('ask the engineer whether...') covering this question either. As written, a reader following the stated budget literally cannot answer the question the step demands they answer — exactly the 'step that cannot be carried out inside its own caps' failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 3 calls out. Fix: either add a handoff ('ask the engineer to confirm source revision, defines, filelist, library/VIP versions and seed match') or narrow the bullet to only what the budgeted Grep can actually surface.
review.open_twice: Largely yes. The methodology is the genuinely valuable part — killing mismatches at 'is this even the same experiment' before anyone opens the standard, degrading gracefully when no comparison file exists, insisting on the divergence point rather than the first printed diff, the requirement/permission/recommendation classification table, and the honest 'implementation-defined does not exist for two modes of our own tool' rule in step 8 are all sharp, correct, hard-won DV judgment calls that read exactly like the golden references. The author also showed real discipline avoiding invented tool names, flags, or clause numbers — every specific fact is properly a [[FILL:]] slot. What would make a senior engineer stop trusting it on a second read: the step-9 instruction to 'write the entry into the Precedent record' when the agent plainly cannot, and hitting the step-1 wall where the procedure asks a question ('same defines, same filelist, same library/VIP versions') its own one-Grep budget cannot answer. Both are fixable without touching the skill's actual judgment content.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean (0 errors, 0 advisories), check_pack returns nothing for this slug, role/level are exactly eda-product-validation-engineer/staff, all nine local slots plus the three cited profile facts are spent, and the DV content is accurate and unusually well informed (the randomisation gotcha correctly separates "the standard pins a reference algorithm for some sources but not all" from "the seeding structure is constrained"; solve-before changes distribution not solution set; self-determined vs context-determined width and unsigned contaminating the context-determined set; same-region process ordering left free; two-state vs four-state not being the same experiment). But I would not hand it to a DV engineer today. Step 1 — the step the skill itself calls the one that kills more reported mismatches than every step after it — Greps for "the tool's own version banner", a string no slot and no profile fact defines, in a pack whose two sibling skills (dv-customer-defect-handoff, dv-tool-version-migration) each declare a local Version banner slot precisely because it cannot be known, and dv-tool-version-migration:66 explicitly warns it is not the profile's Simulator row. The agent must guess a pattern, and one of the two sides is another vendor's tool. Compounding it, the same step's verification demands "both target editions ... quoted from the outputs themselves" while step 1 states its Grep "shows three things and no more" and has no Read — so that evidence is unobtainable inside the budget. And step 3's human-driven bisection reads two new outputs outside the declared "Eight Greps, five Reads", where the sibling dv-minimal-reproducer solves the identical problem by pricing its budget per iteration.
remaining: BLOCKER — Greps for an undefined marker (standing rule 4). Line 130: 'each pattern alternating three things: the tool's own version banner, the profile's Run identity string and the profile's Pass marker.' Run identity and Pass marker are profile facts; the version banner string is defined by no slot, and _shared/team-profile.md:67 carries only **Simulator** ('which simulator we use, and the command that launches a build'), which dv-tool-version-migration:66 states in as many words is NOT the banner fact. The banner is then required verbatim (line 134 'Quote both version banners verbatim'), carried into the block ('runs : <both run identities, both version banners, ...>'), and made a verification item (line 416). Both dv-customer-defect-handoff (slot table row 'Version banner') and dv-tool-version-migration (row 'Version banners') declare it locally. Worse here than in either: one of the two sides is another vendor's tool, whose banner our profile could never record. FIX: add a local slot, e.g. 'Version banners | [[FILL: what each side prints to identify its own version, and where in each output that line appears — including the other vendor's tool]] | validation lead', with the usual 'this is not the profile's Fatal markers' note.

BLOCKER — 'both target editions' has no retrieval anywhere in the budget. Line 135-137: 'The Grep above shows three things and no more: the version banners, the run identity and the pass marker ... this step has no Read to spend.' Yet line 147 says 'Record both targets now', the block asks for 'both target editions', and line 416 requires 'both version banners and both target editions are quoted **from the outputs themselves**'. The **Standard and edition** slot's second half ('where each side of a comparison records the edition it targets') is therefore never spent by any Grep or Read — the slot is half-dead and the verification item is unsatisfiable as written. FIX: either fold the edition marker into step 1's alternation (making it four things, and correcting 'three things and no more' plus the Grep count), or drop 'from the outputs themselves' for the edition and say plainly it comes from the slot for our side and from the engineer for theirs.

BLOCKER — step 3's bisection loop spends retrieval outside the declared budget. Line 185-186: 'ask the engineer to repeat both runs ... and to give you the two new paths. That bisection is a loop a human drives; the agent proposes the window and reads the result.' Reading two new outputs costs at least two more Greps (budget rule 3 forbids opening an output with Read first) and two more Reads, against line 106's 'Eight Greps, five Reads' and rule 4's 'The whole budget, and nothing outside it'. With the five-Read stopping rule (rule 8), a skill that bisects once can no longer afford step 4's two Reads plus step 6's one — so the procedure cannot be completed inside its own caps. The pack already has the answer: dv-minimal-reproducer prices its budget 'Per shrink iteration' and names the groups that sit outside it. FIX: price one bisection iteration explicitly, or say the reduced pair re-enters step 3 under a fresh budget.

Step 8 arithmetic and enumeration are both wrong. 'Two modes of one product cannot rule `implementation-defined` ... Striking that one ruling out leaves three, and all three are live' — the ruling enum has six tokens, so striking one leaves five; and the first of the three bullets (the Mode semantics documented-difference case) is not a ruling token at all. `standard-ambiguity` is live for two modes of one product (a silent clause is silent regardless of how many implementations exist) and is silently dropped, and `testcase-error` / `not-comparable` are reachable for same-tool pairs via steps 5 and 1. As written the step tells someone adjudicating two modes of our own tool that only three outcomes exist, which pushes same-tool mismatches toward `tool-bug` or `unspecified-behaviour`.

`clause says` has no token for 'no clause was opened', yet three of the six rulings are assigned before step 7 ever runs: `not-comparable` at step 1 ('record `ruling: not-comparable` and stop'), and `testcase-error` and `unspecified-behaviour` at step 5, a step whose own title is 'Clear the confounders **before opening the standard**'. Human verification then requires '`clause says` carries the token step 7's table maps that row to', which is unsatisfiable for all three. The pack's habit everywhere else is an explicit honesty token (`not-read`, `not-run`, and this very block's own `record-not-readable`); `clause says` needs one, e.g. `not-opened`.

Internal contradiction on clause evidence. Step 5 item 5 rules `unspecified-behaviour` from a race with no clause at all ('Both orders are legal; this is `ruling: unspecified-behaviour`'), while step 8 says `unspecified-behaviour` 'needs the same clause evidence as any other ruling, not a shrug about scheduling'. One of the two has to give.

Minor — `precedent : <matching entry key> | not-matched | record-not-readable` cannot express one of the two non-answers step 6 distinguishes. Step 6 separates 'the record is not a file that can be read' (check pending) from 'the slot is unfilled' (the check did not happen); only the first has a token, so an unfilled Precedent record slot gets written as `record-not-readable`, which claims a record exists.

Minor — `runs` promises 'both seeds' but no step obtains a seed value. Budget rule 5 states the seed 'appear[s] in none of the three markers step 1 greps for', and step 1's ask is phrased as confirmation that the seeds *match*, not disclosure of what they are. Either ask for the values or drop them from the field.

Note, not a defect against the pack as it stands — 442 lines against the stated 180-260 target. The pack has drifted here (dv-minimal-reproducer 448, dv-tool-release-behaviour-diff 392, golden reference dv-ral-bringup 359), so this is a norm question rather than something to fix in this skill alone. Nothing in the file reads as padding.
